subject: Region hosting & private endpoint evidence for MedVita PII workloads
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <security@medvita.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 16:14:00 +0200
Subject: Request: Region hosting & private endpoint evidence for MedVita PII workloads

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this — MedVita is evaluating Redwood for a pilot that will process patient-identifiable data for EU patients. Our security team has a short set of asks so we can complete the SIG/CAIQ review and confirm we meet our internal data residency controls. Can you confirm the following by next Thursday (2026-05-13)?

1) Which exact regions host customer inference workloads for the EU offering (region names + cloud regions; we need the geographic boundary statement).
2) For Private/managed VPC deployment: do you support customer-initiated VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, or a Redwood-managed private connector? Please include IP ranges, egress control model, and whether traffic ever transits a public internet path.
3) KMS model: can customers supply a customer-managed key (CMK) that is isolated per account/tenant? Is there a KMS partitioning guarantee?
4) Audit logs: retention and proof of immutable audit (S3 object lock / append-only logging) and whether logs for inference requests can be exported to customer logging endpoints.
5) SOC 2 Type II / CAIQ: a pointer to the latest SOC 2 report and a completed CAIQ/SSP (if you can provide a redacted copy).

If you can provide a short packet (PDF + a one-page bullet summary), we will attach it to the procurement package. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if that’s easier — Alex Carter (cc) is our architect and will validate the network details.

Appreciate it,

Elena Rossi
Head of Security, MedVita Health

--
MedVita Health
security@medvita.com
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <security@medvita.com>
Cc: Alex Carter <alex.carter@medvita.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Region hosting & private endpoint evidence for MedVita PII workloads

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. We can get you everything you asked for. High-level answers up front and then I’ll attach a short evidence pack: redwood-private-endpoint-runbook.pdf and eu-hosting-statement.txt.

- Regions: EU workloads are served from our eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 clusters. For APAC pilot options we have ap-southeast-1 availability; we can constrain inference to a single region per account.
- Private connectivity: we support customer-managed VPC peering (route-based), AWS PrivateLink endpoints, and a Redwood Private Connector (managed transit with customer-controlled peering). Traffic to inference hosts never routes over the public internet once a private connection is established.
- KMS: customer-managed CMKs are supported; you can scope a key per account. We also offer per-tenant key partitioning for Private deployments.
- Audit logs: inference request logs can be exported to customer S3 or a customer logging endpoint; we retain audit logs for 365 days by default and provide options for longer retention. Immutable exports can be provided using S3 Object Lock; see attached runbook for the export step.
- SOC 2 / CAIQ: we will provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II and a completed CAIQ snapshot in the evidence bundle.

I’m looping in Marcus (infra) and Monica (compliance) to add concrete artifacts and confirm the diagram/IPs. Will follow up with the bundle by Monday.

Best,

Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments:
- redwood-private-endpoint-runbook.pdf (runbook, 6 pages)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 8 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: VPC peering/IP ranges and audit export details (MedVita)

Internal note — drafting the technical snippets to include in the bundle. Keeping this internal until we include the redacted IPs for public distribution.

Summary of technical controls for the packet:

- Regions and AZs: eu-west-1 (multiple AZs: eu-west-1a/b/c) and eu-central-1 (a/b). APAC pilot: ap-southeast-1. We pin inference clusters by region/tenant.
- Private connectivity modes supported:
  * Customer VPC Peering: BGP-less static routing, route table entries; we publish recommended route prefixes per deployment (example ranges provided in the internal diagram).
  * AWS PrivateLink: endpoint services offered; traffic stays in the AWS control plane and does not touch public internet.
  * Redwood Private Connector: managed transit option for customers that prefer a Redwood-facing managed connector; logs and routing are exported to customer endpoints.
- IP / CIDR handling: we require at least a /27 of dedicated CIDR for each peering session; public CIDR is never used when PrivateLink or peering is configured. Exact customer-facing prefixes will be redacted in the public bundle.
- KMS and key partitioning: supports customer-managed CMKs (AWS KMS). For Private deployments we support customer-provided HSM-backed keys; keys are not exported from the region.
- Audit/export: we support two modes — direct push to customer S3 (with optional S3 Object Lock) or push to a customer SIEM via secure TLS connection. Logs are hashed and retained 365 days; on request we can extend retention or provide streamed copies for archival.

I attached the network diagram we will include in the bundle. Please confirm redaction policy for IPs before I publish the bundle to the shared drive.

Marcus Lin
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments (internal): network-diagram-vpc.pdf (diagram, include redacted ranges)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>

Subject: Final evidence packet for MedVita — regions, VPC modes, KMS, and logs

Hi Elena / Alex,

Thanks for the patience — attached is a concise evidence bundle for your procurement pack. Highlights below and a couple of items where we request confirmation from your side.

Attached: medvita-evidence-bundle.zip (contains a redacted SOC 2 Type II cover page, completed CAIQ snapshot, redwood-private-endpoint-runbook.pdf, eu-hosting-statement.txt, network-diagram-vpc.pdf)

Quick summary:
- Regions: EU inference is available from eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. APAC pilot available in ap-southeast-1; we can pin workloads to a single region and enforce egress in-region.
- Private connectivity: we support VPC peering (route-based), AWS PrivateLink, and a Redwood Private Connector. Once a private connection is established, inference traffic does not traverse the public internet.
- KMS: customer-managed CMKs are supported; for Private deployments we offer customer HSM-backed keys. Keys are created in-region and not moved across regions.
- Audit logs: default retention 365 days, exportable to customer S3 with S3 Object Lock for immutability or to a customer logging endpoint. We can provide hashed request logs and replay artifacts for a given window on request.

Actions for MedVita:
- Please confirm whether you prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink for the pilot (our recommended default is PrivateLink for simpler routing).
- Confirm the target region for the pilot (eu-west-1 or eu-central-1).
- If you require extended log retention or different export cadence, indicate desired retention window and destination.

If it helps, I’m available for a 20-minute technical sync with Alex and your network/security engineers. We can also provide a short on-site run-through of the Private Connector behavior and failover runbook.

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
